purpose.summary: Classify the repeated hosted mixed-node failure using only closed lifecycle and feature-frame identifiers without exposing child output.
scope: Load the unchanged matrix driver from exact technical commit 889212482c964ec98dcc2ac55321cb0e04e17666 and require its four canonical scenarios and mixed-node lifecycle markers to remain exact.

Call the immutable output validator exactly once and, when it rejects the mixed-node child output, report only a closed failure kind, the last valid completed lifecycle prefix and the last traceback frame belonging to an exact feature-function allowlist.
Classify mixed-node MatrixError failures raised before output validation as before-output-validation with no lifecycle or feature-frame claim.
Reject duplicate, non-prefix or out-of-order lifecycle marker states and never infer causality or a root cause from the last completed lifecycle or allowlisted frame.
Keep the technical target, scenario execution, successful reproduction, receipt, comparison, cleanup and promotion behavior unchanged.
exclusions: No workflow, container, dependency, production-node build, node, consensus, validation, P2P, storage, RPC, wallet, Chronik, activation, testnet, mainnet, or operator-binary change.
No modification of the accepted ERGON-CHANGE-0010 technical target, matrix bytes, scenarios, functional scripts, inherited selection, existing report or semantic projection.
No child stdout, stderr, traceback, line number, command, path, port, environment, secret, return code or free-form error text is retained or printed.
No reported lifecycle or feature frame is a causal diagnosis, failed-function claim or root-cause claim.
No retry, incoming evidence, workflow artifact, proof promotion, deterministic-build claim, public-network claim or mainnet-coexistence claim.

limitations: Publishing this diagnostic change does not reproduce ERGON-CHANGE-0010 and does not promote evidence.

The bounded diagnostic identifies only a closed failure kind, last valid completed lifecycle and last allowlisted feature frame; it intentionally does not expose the assertion, traceback, process output, path, port, environment or root cause.
The last completed lifecycle and allowlisted feature frame are location hints only and do not prove which operation or function caused the failure.

A successful future hosted comparison can cover only the existing bounded synthetic regtest matrix; it cannot establish deterministic builds, operator-binary equivalence, historical-chain replay, public-network peering, sustained operation or mainnet coexistence.
The ERGON-CHANGE-0010 report remains Observed with an assembled-component ceiling until a separate accepted evidence promotion binds an independent successful execution.
counterevidence: Public workflow_dispatch run 33901994571 attempt 1, job 101118019944, on exact diagnostic commit b4ed65c87fff2713856c1f50f6bd95bc7e6ed5c5 completed failure after both fresh builds in scenario mixed-node-coexistence, emitted no report or artifact, and exposed no narrower failure category.

A second fresh public workflow_dispatch run 33910672119 attempt 1, job 101146103339, on the same exact commit repeated the mixed-node-coexistence failure after both fresh builds and again emitted no report or artifact.

An exact maintainer-local digest-pinned Ubuntu 22.04 ARM64 container run passed all four scenarios with fresh clones and builds, but remains local Observed evidence; the repeatable GitHub-hosted-only failure is unresolved and forbids promotion.
The new classifier does not diagnose or fix the failure and cannot turn a failed run into evidence.
